$comment: Single source of truth for the Carousel API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: carousel
title: Carousel
description: Slides you can swipe through, with previous and next buttons, dots and arrow keys.

label.description: Names the carousel, e.g. "Featured stays". Required.

children.description: One child per slide. Each is wrapped in a slide labelled "1 of 4".

perView.description: How many slides show at once. Fractions show a peek of the next one. On narrow screens it drops to at most 2, then about 1.2.

dots.description: A dot for each slide. Turn off for many slides or several per view.

controls.description: Previous and next buttons. Swiping, scrolling and arrow keys work either way.

onSlideChange.description: Called with the first fully shown slide (0-based).

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: One slide at a time. Swipe, scroll with a trackpad, use the buttons or dots, or focus it and press the arrow keys. In HTML, add data-vin-carousel and include vinui.js.

examples.title: Several per view
examples.description: Three cards at a time (fewer on small screens), no dots.

a11y: Follows the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern: a section with aria-roledescription="carousel" and a label, and slides with role="group", aria-roledescription="slide" and a label like "1 of 4".
No autoplay, so nothing moves unless the person moves it. The slides are a polite live region, so a screen reader reads the new slide.
Slides that are out of view are inert: Tab skips their links and screen readers skip their text.
Previous and Next are buttons with names; at the ends they get aria-disabled="true" (not disabled), so focus never gets lost.
The dots are buttons named "Slide 1", "Slide 2"…, and the current one has aria-current="true". Each dot's hit area is 24 by 24 pixels.
The slide track is a native scroll-snap scroller, so touch swipe and trackpads work without JavaScript. It can be focused, and the arrow keys move one slide.
With reduced motion on, slides jump instead of gliding.
